classes.name: TNF inhibitors

starting.description: In the rheumatoid therapeutic-antibody branch, synovial cultures spontaneously produced TNF and IL-1 and neutralizing TNF reduced IL-1 production, supporting a therapeutic hypothesis; osteoarthritis cultures differed. In a distinct receptor-Fc branch, urine-derived TNF-inhibitory proteins furnished observed functional precedents for the 1991 receptor-IgG design; the authors explicitly cite earlier 1989 urinary studies. Beutler also describes observed TNF/LPS biology as the reason to block TNF. The 1988 inhibitory activity was not assigned to the specific TBPII protein.

inspiration.description: Endogenous TNF and observed TNF-dependent inflammatory cytokine production in rheumatoid synovial cultures; separately, naturally occurring soluble TNF inhibitors from body fluids and observed TNF-associated inflammatory shock informed receptor-Fc development.

steps.description: Rheumatoid synovial cells spontaneously produced inflammatory cytokines; blocking endogenous TNF reduced IL-1 production in culture, unlike the low-IL-1 osteoarthritis comparator in the original abstract.

The team used the TNF-regulation hypothesis to pursue an early clinical rheumatoid arthritis study with the preexisting chimeric anti-TNF antibody cA2; anti-TNF therapies subsequently included adalimumab.

A separate antibody engineering program used MAK 195 to guide phage-display selection of human antibody chains and affinity optimization, yielding the D2E7 anti-TNF candidate in rheumatoid arthritis clinical development; D2E7 is adalimumab.

In a distinct receptor-Fc branch, an earlier urinary IL-1 inhibitory activity led investigators to search for and observe TNF-inhibitory activity in febrile patients' urine. A later study cited the observation, isolated two TNF-binding proteins, and proposed therapeutic applications. The 1988 study did not identify its inhibitory factor as TBPII.

Peppel and colleagues explicitly proposed derivatives of naturally occurring soluble TNF inhibitors and engineered a p55 receptor-mouse-IgG fusion to address fragment limitations. Beutler later described their p55/p75 fusion work and related the p75 product to etanercept; Novick describes etanercept as a modified TBPII-Fc fusion. These accounts do not establish that the p55 experimental construct was itself etanercept.

design.description: Researchers moved a chimeric TNF-neutralizing antibody into a planned clinical test. Separately, the D2E7/adalimumab team used a murine anti-TNF template for phage-display guided selection of human counterparts and affinity optimization. The receptor branch addressed the limitations of naturally occurring receptor fragments by engineering a bivalent IgG fusion.

circumstances.description: The early anti-TNF clinical test and D2E7 antibody-engineering program were planned. Novick's detailed account calls isolation of the second urinary TNF-binding protein unexpected, although her abstract calls both TNF receptors expected; this inconsistency remains unresolved.

limits: The documented therapeutic-antibody history centers on rheumatoid arthritis and the sole cohort member, adalimumab. The murine MAK 195-guided D2E7 lineage is not asserted to descend molecularly from the separate chimeric cA2/infliximab antibody.

The anti-TNF antibody cA2 had been developed for septic shock before the rheumatoid arthritis study; the earlier sepsis antibody program is not reconstructed, and the rheumatoid culture findings did not create all anti-TNF research.

The receptor-Fc branch is distinct from the antibody format. The original receptor-Fc experiment establishes direct inspiration from earlier urinary and serum inhibitory proteins, but used p55 and mouse IgG; the connection of p75 to etanercept is attributed to later discoverer accounts. Etanercept is not a cohort member.
Small-molecule TNF modulators were not traced or classified here; no shared molecular template or universal origin is assumed for all TNF-targeting modalities.
conflicts: Novick 2022 describes both TNF receptors as expected in the abstract, but calls TBPII unexpected and serendipitous in the detailed 'Soluble TNF receptors (1989)' section. The conflict concerns expectation, not the reported existence of two binding proteins; no resolution is established.
gaps: The 1989 original rheumatoid synovial experiment was read only at abstract extent; detailed methods and full results were not accessed.
The 1998 D2E7 account is a conference abstract, not a full methods article; its identity as adalimumab is supplied by the MRC institutional exhibit.

Neither the D2E7 conference abstract nor the MRC exhibit establishes that the specific 1989 rheumatoid synovial experiment directly prompted the BASF/CAT program; the connection is at the level of known TNF inflammatory biology and the wider therapeutic class.

The 1988 partially purified inhibitory activity is not assigned to either specific 1990 urinary protein. The 1991 original receptor-Fc paper reports a p55/mouse-IgG construct rather than the final p75/human-IgG product; exact product-specific engineering and the earlier cA2 sepsis antibody program were not reconstructed.

classes.name: Bisphosphonates

starting.description: Biological fluids contained an inhibitor of calcium phosphate precipitation, partly identified as inorganic pyrophosphate; its effects on calcium phosphate crystals and its rapid breakdown motivated the search for stable analogues. Observation of inhibited crystal dissolution then led to tests of bone resorption.

inspiration.description: Endogenous inorganic pyrophosphate and observations of inhibited calcium-phosphate crystal formation and dissolution; later the observed effect of synthetic bisphosphonates on crystal dissolution supported tests of bone resorption. Dental research on etidronate formed a convergent strand, with a reported unexpected effect of the synthetic compound on rat bone mineralization.

steps.description: Studies of inhibitors in biological fluids identified pyrophosphate as a contributor to inhibition of calcium phosphate precipitation and showed effects on crystal formation and dissolution.

Researchers sought enzyme-stable analogues retaining pyrophosphate-like activity; previously known industrial bisphosphonates met these criteria. Francis's dental research formed a convergent strand; safety testing of etidronate also revealed an unexpected inhibition of rat bone mineralization, distinct from antiresorption.

The observed inhibition of hydroxyapatite dissolution by pyrophosphate and bisphosphonates prompted tests of bone resorption, a distinct biological endpoint; the 1969 abstract reports inhibition in tissue culture and rats.

Etidronate was used clinically for pathological ectopic calcification; subsequent medicinal chemistry and empirical biological tests produced more potent antiresorptive compounds, including amino-containing alendronate. Later work differentiated the intracellular mechanisms of nitrogen-containing agents from those of some earlier compounds.

design.description: Researchers sought hydrolysis-resistant analogues retaining pyrophosphate-like physicochemical activity and applied an existing synthetic chemical family to the biological problem. Later synthesis and empirical screening of side-chain variants produced more potent nitrogen-containing drugs, including alendronate; their intracellular enzyme target was identified later. This was more than a delivery adjustment, but not evidence that the class was designed from scratch.

circumstances.description: The search for hydrolysis-resistant pyrophosphate analogues was planned. Separately, a retrospective describes an unexpected inhibition of rat bone mineralization during etidronate toothpaste-safety tests; that finding was not itself the test of bone resorption.

limits: The pyrophosphate-to-stable-analogue and antiresorption chain is supported at class level; this does not establish every later analogue's individual discovery history.

Francis's dental research was a convergent strand; the reported safety-test finding concerned impaired bone mineralization, not discovery of the antiresorption endpoint. The contemporaneous report behind the safety-test account was not read.
The original 1969 bone-resorption paper was accessible only as an abstract and reproduced introduction and conclusion fragments; its full experimental methods and results were not read.
conflicts: S5 describes an early fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva case series in strongly positive terms (E13), whereas S1 expressed caution in 1998 about the overall evidence for efficacy in ectopic ossification, including that condition (E16). Case-level impressions and a later assessment of the evidence are not necessarily contradictory; the underlying clinical report was not read and no efficacy conclusion is made here.
gaps: Full text of the 1962 urinary-pyrophosphate report and the complete 1969 bone-resorption experiment was not accessed; their abstracts and the latter's reproduced fragments were read.
The primary paper cited for the etidronate dental-safety animal observation and the early clinical case report were not read; these details are attributed to the 2021 historical review.

Original discovery and clinical-development papers specific to alendronate were not reviewed; the class-level history and later structure–activity account do not establish its individual priority or chronology.

classes.name: Xanthine oxidase inhibitors

starting.description: Observed 6-MP conversion to 6-thiouric acid by xanthine oxidase suggested inhibiting that metabolic pathway to potentiate the anticancer drug. A prior enzyme screen had found activity for the synthetic hypoxanthine analogue allopurinol, which was selected for testing in vivo.

inspiration.description: Observed 6-MP metabolism and the previously observed enzyme-inhibiting effect of synthetic allopurinol motivated the experimental program; the relationship between the enzyme and uric acid production opened the clinical application. Allopurinol is a hypoxanthine analogue, but analogue identity alone does not establish the initial molecular design motivation.

steps.description: Metabolic studies revealed 6-MP oxidation, and earlier screening of purine analogues identified allopurinol as a xanthine oxidase inhibitor.
Investigators selected allopurinol to test in-vivo enzyme inhibition and 6-MP potentiation; subsequent decreases in uric acid suggested gout treatment.
Subsequent studies identified oxypurinol as an inhibitory metabolite and investigated allopurinol in patients with gout and hyperuricemia, including a comparative clinical study.

design.description: Falco prepared the synthetic hypoxanthine analogue; researchers screened purine-related structures, selected an enzyme-active compound, and deliberately tested its effect on 6-MP metabolism in vivo. The same inhibitor was then investigated for a different therapeutic use. Oxypurinol was identified as an enzyme-generated active metabolite, not a separately designed founding branch.

circumstances.description: The specific in-vivo selection and test of an already enzyme-active compound to reduce 6-MP oxidation were planned. Rundles describes the overall development route as serendipitous in an abstract; it does not specify which event was unexpected, so the planned value is not a blanket claim about the route or the gout application.

classes.name: Benzodiazepines

starting.description: An empirical tranquilizer search yielded an unexpected animal pharmacology profile for the synthetic compound later named chlordiazepoxide; its promising effects prompted synthesis of related benzodiazepines.

inspiration.description: Unexpected sedative, muscle-relaxant and anticonvulsant animal effects of the synthetic chlordiazepoxide lead prompted further development. Upstream, natural alkaloids were among the examples behind a broad basic-amine design heuristic, alongside synthetic drugs; they were not identified as natural molecular precursors of the benzodiazepine lead.

steps.description: The group pursued a deliberate empirical chemical search for a new tranquilizer, selecting chemistry familiar from earlier dyestuff work.
An untested synthetic sample was submitted for pharmacological screening in 1957 and showed an unexpectedly promising animal-test profile; this effect motivated synthesis of analogues.
Structural investigation revealed that an unexpected chemical rearrangement had formed the 1,4-benzodiazepine ring; the active lead became chlordiazepoxide.
An active decomposition product and subsequent molecular modifications yielded diazepam, selected for higher potency in tests.

Upjohn researchers subsequently developed triazolobenzodiazepines by modifying the established 1,4-benzodiazepine system and testing the new compounds against diazepam analogues; the 1971 series included the compound later named alprazolam.

design.description: Researchers synthesized and screened the initial compound, elucidated and modified the active chemical series, and selected a more potent 1-methyl derivative for development as diazepam.

circumstances.description: The search for a tranquilizer and the 1957 animal screening were planned; the positive pharmacological result for the stored compound was unexpected.

Sternbach distinguishes Roche's clonazepam from Wyeth's lorazepam as later analogues. Upjohn's alprazolam is a later triazolobenzodiazepine; its detailed internal research decisions are not reconstructed as a separate class founding.

conflicts: The 2005 review S7 describes chlordiazepoxide as emerging from side-chain work within chlorpromazine's structure (E14). Sternbach's oral history instead distinguishes an earlier unproductive phenothiazine effort from his later intention to seek a new group unrelated to Thorazine (E15). classes.name: Tricyclic antidepressants

starting.description: In antipsychotic testing of synthetic G 22355, agitation or hypomania suggested a mood-elevating effect. A participant retrospectively links this mood change to a proposal to test depression; some patients with prominent depressive features also improved. Kuhn recalls that electroshock responses had encouraged his belief that a drug treatment was possible.

inspiration.description: Observed mood and depressive-symptom changes in patients receiving synthetic G 22355, followed by intentional testing in depression; Kuhn also recalled clinical response to electroshock as prior evidence of treatment potential. Ayd says Kuhn's reported imipramine effects and structural resemblance partly motivated his search for antidepressant activity of amitriptyline, and his own observations led him to test it in patients diagnosed with depression. No natural molecular template is asserted.

steps.description: Geigy made iminodibenzyl derivatives during a search for novel antihistamines; after chlorpromazine's clinical success, the team tested G 22355 as a possible antipsychotic.

According to a participant retrospective, hypomanic mood elevation during schizophrenia testing led to a proposal to test depression; some patients with depressive features also improved. Kuhn recalled that prior electroshock responses suggested to him that a drug treatment could exist, and agreed with a leading interview question about the role of mood elevation.
Kuhn described antidepressant responses and differing effects on schizophrenic symptoms in his original 1958 clinical paper; the mechanism was not then known.

Ayd recalls that imipramine's reported antidepressant effect and structural resemblance prompted him to look for such effects with amitriptyline. His initial clinical observations were followed by a deliberate test in people diagnosed with depression. A review describes thioxanthene-based Merck work and separately describes Roche and Lundbeck modifying imipramine to synthesize amitriptyline; the complete development and priority sequence remains unresolved.

design.description: Researchers prepared and screened iminodibenzyl derivatives, interpreted patient responses and deliberately tested depression. The review describes central-ring changes from thioxanthenes in one amitriptyline route and modifying imipramine in another; Ayd recalls using structural resemblance to guide his clinical search. The complete synthesis and company-priority sequence is not established here.

circumstances.description: The Geigy screen for antipsychotic activity was planned; the unexpected mood elevation supplied the clue for proposing a depression trial, while some patients with depressive features also improved. The subsequent depression tests, including Ayd's amitriptyline investigation following observed activity, were deliberate.

Ayd describes the latter as informed by imipramine's effect and structural resemblance. The review reports both a thioxanthene-based route and a Roche/Lundbeck imipramine-modification route, but their detailed chronology and motivations are not established here.
The class boundary excludes tricyclic skeletal-muscle relaxants. No exhaustive analysis of every later antidepressant analogue is attempted.

Ayd recalls a Roche synthesis for possible antipsychotic use; its relationship to the review's chemistry narrative and the full company-priority sequence remain unverified.

The participant retrospectives do not establish the precise priority of the depression-test proposal; Kuhn's agreement that high mood suggested the idea followed a leading interview question.

classes.name: Dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers

starting.description: The reported coronary vasodilating effect of the plant-derived compound khellin was the starting point for Bossert's search for a usable coronary vasodilator.

inspiration.description: A reported biological effect of khellin, a plant-derived coronary vasodilator, supplied the starting point.

steps.description: Khellin's reported coronary vasodilator effect provided Bossert's starting point for a search for a suitable coronary vasodilator.

Bossert and Vater pursued khellin-type cardioactive compounds with improved activity and solubility through changes in molecular skeleton; a route through quinolones and fused dihydropyridines yielded coronary-active Hantzsch-type dihydropyridines.

In a contemporaneous independent SmithKline and French line, investigators reportedly observed hypotensive activity of an injected dihydropyridine in dogs and then sought orally active analogues; the line's relation to the assigned medicines is not established.

A 2-nitrophenyl member of the Bayer series was synthesized and selected as nifedipine, with coronary activity disclosed in a 1969 patent; calcium-entry inhibition was identified after the cardiovascular effects, and the active class prompted further chemical investigation.

design.description: Researchers altered the khellin-type skeleton in pursuit of activity and solubility, produced a distinct coronary-active dihydropyridine series and selected the nifedipine candidate; the final structure was synthetic rather than a compound isolated from the plant.

circumstances.description: The search for an effective coronary vasodilator and modification of khellin-type structures are described as planned. The inventors' patent calls the series' long-lasting oral or intravenous coronary dilation a surprising discovery; that is patent language, not independent evidence of the investigators' subjective state. The status of the original khellin observation is not established.

classes.name: Penicillins

starting.description: On an accidentally mould-contaminated staphylococcal culture plate, nearby bacteria were observed undergoing lysis. Fleming subcultured the mould and developed its diffusible antibacterial activity into the named penicillin culture filtrate, which he studied for bacterial selection and possible treatment.

inspiration.description: A mould-produced diffusible antibacterial substance and the observed lysis of staphylococci near its colony.

steps.description: Fleming noticed bacterial lysis around a contaminating mould and investigated the resulting antibacterial mould-culture filtrate.
Fleming demonstrated selective use in bacteriological cultures and suggested possible therapeutic application.
Oxford researchers developed injectable penicillin as systemic chemotherapy and demonstrated activity in mice, stimulating subsequent clinical use, according to Rolinson's retrospective.
The phenoxymethylpenicillin branch provided an acid-stable oral penicillin. A 1988 institutional report describes production by mould fermentation with a phenoxyacetic acid precursor.

Fermentation and assay work yielded 6-APA, the nucleus to which new side chains could be attached. Semisynthetic branches sought wider activity, oral absorption, or penicillinase stability; these include amoxicillin and flucloxacillin.

design.description: Researchers cultivated the mould and developed an active filtrate, established systemic experimental treatment, used precursor-fed fermentation for penicillin V production, and recovered 6-APA for side-chain changes to improve absorption, broaden activity or improve stability against penicillinase.

circumstances.description: The plate contamination and associated lysis were unexpected observations during staphylococcal work; the mould subculture and examination of its diffusible activity were deliberate follow-up.

classes.name: Beta-lactamase inhibitors

starting.description: Recognized bacterial penicillinase-mediated antibiotic destruction and prior β-lactamase inhibition by a microbial metabolite, cephalosporin C, supported a purposeful microbial search for inhibitors; the observed activity of a S. clavuligerus culture supplied the clavulanic acid lead.

inspiration.description: Bacterial β-lactamase-mediated resistance and inhibition by the microbial metabolite cephalosporin C provided a rationale and precedent for the microbial search; a distinct natural product isolated from S. clavuligerus supplied the clavulanic acid lead. Observed effects of semisynthetic penicillins motivated a parallel screen of existing compounds, not a claim that clavulanic acid itself was derived from them.

steps.description: Observed bacterial destruction of penicillins and inhibition of penicillinase by a microbial metabolite and some semisynthetic penicillins established the protecting-inhibitor rationale.
In a parallel line, investigators screened semisynthetic penicillins for better inhibition; a promising lead proved poorly absorbed orally.
Rolinson began a synergy screen for natural inhibitors in 1967; the programme initially found unstable olivanic-acid activity.
A cephamycin-related hypothesis led the team to grow S. clavuligerus, where chromatography detected the distinct inhibitory product later named clavulanic acid.

The team pursued a penicillin-plus-inhibitor strategy; the observed inhibitor lowered the in-vitro antibiotic concentrations needed against several resistant strains, and favorable oral absorption was discovered during development.
Clavulanic acid was introduced in an amoxicillin combination in 1981, followed by a ticarcillin combination.

design.description: Researchers designed and adapted the synergy screen, selected and cultured a producer organism, separated the inhibitor from culture fluid, and planned penicillin-plus-inhibitor therapy. The lead's biological activity and favorable absorption were observed rather than specified de novo.

circumstances.description: The search for microbial enzyme inhibitors and the therapeutic combination were planned. Cole describes obtaining a culture to explore cephamycins but identifying a different inhibitor, and Doyle calls the compatible oral absorption a fortunate finding.

classes.name: Amphetamine-type CNS stimulants

starting.description: Known oral and clinical effects of the Ephedra alkaloid ephedrine motivated an ephedrine-substitute program. Subsequently observed amphetamine-related wakefulness became a clue for stimulant clinical use; the historian also considers prior ephedrine experience a possible influence on narcolepsy testing.

inspiration.description: A naturally occurring ephedrine lead and its observed physiological and clinical effects guided the substitute search; subsequent amphetamine observations informed stimulant use.

steps.description: The Ephedra alkaloid ephedrine produced circulatory and bronchial effects in animal studies. Clinically useful oral ephedrine effects and constrained supply motivated a search for a substitute.
Alles prepared ephedrine-related candidates; amphetamine sulfate had oral and pressor activity in animals and produced wakefulness in his self-test.

Alles supplied amphetamine for narcolepsy trials; the historian identifies observed wakefulness and ephedrine experience as clues. The 1935 clinical authors explicitly cite awakening animals and insomnia in humans as reasons to explore stimulant use.

In a distinct pediatric behavioral application, Bradley reported observations during Benzedrine treatment in 1937 and suggested medically supervised use for behavior disorders; the historical diagnostic group is not assumed identical to modern ADHD.
After comparative observations showed stronger central activity of the dextro isomer, Prinzmetal and Alles investigated it clinically in conditions responsive to the racemate.

The later L-lysine-d-amphetamine prodrug conjugated the established active dextro drug to lysine to alter its delivery; the patent describes synthesis and preclinical comparison. An FDA review identifies its dimethanesulfonate salt as lisdexamfetamine dimesylate.

design.description: Alles prepared and tested ephedrine-related synthetic compounds, including phenylisopropylamine sulfate. Investigators resolved amphetamine into optical isomers and compared the dextro form clinically. Later, inventors conjugated active d-amphetamine to L-lysine in a prodrug intended to modify delivery and reduce abuse liability; the FDA identified its salt as lisdexamfetamine dimesylate and advised that labeling reflect high abuse liability.

circumstances.description: The ephedrine-substitute search and testing of the candidate were planned; whether its particular initial stimulant effects were unexpected is not established by this account.

classes.name: Direct factor Xa inhibitors

starting.description: There was no single documented start for every program. Natural inhibitors, including antistasin, showed factor Xa inhibition and anticoagulant activity; discoverers describe natural-inhibitor studies as preceding the later focus on small-molecule inhibitors. Rivaroxaban arose from a targeted screen with active synthetic hits. Separately, a recognized biological sequence similarity prompted the apixaban team's screening of a platelet-inhibitor library; active isoxazolines became its leads. In the Daiichi branch, a working synthetic inhibitor, DX-9065a, prompted later non-amidine research, although the original clue for that earlier program remains unestablished.

inspiration.description: Natural-factor studies supplied target-feasibility evidence; recognition of factor Xa's biological substrate relationship helped motivate one library screen. Observed activities of synthetic screening hits and of the DX-9065a prototype provided later starting points for medicinal-chemistry programs. These are distinct links, not a claim that all oral inhibitors derive structurally from antistasin.

steps.description: In 1987 antistasin, purified from a leech salivary gland extract in antimetastatic research, was observed to inhibit factor Xa and coagulation; the authors hypothesized an Xa-mediated anticoagulant mechanism.

Discoverer retrospectives describe natural-inhibitor studies as evidence for the target and a subsequent focus on small-molecule direct inhibitors; they do not claim a shared natural chemical scaffold.
In the rivaroxaban branch, factor Xa assays of a chemical collection yielded active hits, which were optimized into the candidate.

In the apixaban branch, recognized sequence similarity motivated screening of an antiplatelet library; active isoxazolines underwent modeling and multiple structural revisions into the bicyclic oral candidate.

In a separate Daiichi program, reported to have started in 1979, the active but poorly orally absorbed DX-9065a prototype preceded structure–activity research and screening of non-amidine compounds; this led to the later oral candidate DU-176b, edoxaban.

design.description: Researchers deliberately screened and redesigned active compounds for inhibition, selectivity, antithrombotic activity and oral availability. In the apixaban branch, structure-based redesign changed the lead architecture into a bicyclic candidate; in the Daiichi branch, replacing basic amidine groups and screening non-amidine compounds led to an oral candidate with measured changes in potency and selectivity as well as absorption.

circumstances.description: The specific events classified as planned are the factor Xa-directed chemical screens and subsequent optimization, including the apixaban library screen and Daiichi non-amidine research; this is not a claim that every earlier observation was anticipated.

classes.name: Second-generation antipsychotics

starting.description: In a tricyclic antidepressant-screening program researchers unexpectedly encountered neuroleptic activity; clozapine was subsequently identified. Its clinical antipsychotic effects without the expected extrapyramidal profile became a benchmark for later drugs. Separately, Janssen recalls pursuing an improved pipamperone, and Otsuka reports that clinical observations with OPC-4392 prompted its aripiprazole branch.

inspiration.description: Unexpected neuroleptic effects among screened synthetic tricyclics, clozapine's observed clinical and receptor-binding profiles, effects of pipamperone and ritanserin, existing neuroleptic chemical leads, and OPC-4392 clinical results and dopamine-autoreceptor biology informed distinct lines of development.

steps.description: During a tricyclic antidepressant screen, researchers unexpectedly observed neuroleptic properties and subsequently identified clozapine.

Clozapine's atypical preclinical and clinical profile challenged an assumed requirement for extrapyramidal effects and became a model for later antipsychotics. A review describes industry attempts to emulate its observed receptor profile and names olanzapine, quetiapine and risperidone as resulting agents.

A later controlled comparison in treatment-resistant patients reported greater response to clozapine than to chlorpromazine plus benztropine, contributing clinical evidence for the benchmark described by Hippius.

In a distinct line, Janssen recalls seeking a more potent version of clinically tested pipamperone and combining the properties of ritanserin and haloperidol. A company researcher's presentation describes a medicinal chemistry program based initially on other established neuroleptics, yielding the serotonin/dopamine antagonist risperidone.
In another branch, Otsuka pursued presynaptic autoreceptor agonism, developed and clinically tested OPC-4392, and used its observed benefits and limitations to inform a subsequent program.

The company deliberately screened for both presynaptic and postsynaptic activities, resulting in aripiprazole; subsequent mechanistic analysis characterized it as a D2 partial agonist. The numbered steps group branches rather than assert that each branch began after the preceding one.

design.description: Researchers sought compounds emulating aspects of clozapine's receptor profile, although Janssen personally denied clozapine influenced him. Janssen built a distinct benzisoxazole series around established neuroleptic leads and selected combined serotonin/dopamine antagonism; he described seeking an improved pipamperone and a combination of ritanserin- and haloperidol-like properties. For aripiprazole, Otsuka sought a different activity profile, combining earlier autoreceptor agonism with stronger postsynaptic antagonism, and screened new compounds accordingly.

circumstances.description: The neuroleptic activity encountered during the antidepressant screen was unexpected; the subsequent aripiprazole search for a combined activity profile was planned after clinical observations with OPC-4392.

classes.name: NSAIDs and aspirin (cyclooxygenase-inhibiting family)

starting.description: There is no single molecular founding clue for this heterogeneous pharmacological family. The salicylate branch drew on reported clinical effects of willow bark and subsequent chemistry of salicin and salicylic acid. The ibuprofen program drew on aspirin's known therapeutic effects and a proposed relationship to suppression of UV erythema. An oxicam program developed from anti-inflammatory effects of synthetic indandiones. Selective COX-2 work drew on observed inducible COX biology and previously active anti-inflammatory lead structures.

inspiration.description: Willow bark and its reported clinical effect anchor the salicylate branch. Known effects of synthetic aspirin, phenylbutazone and active indandione or diarylpyrazole leads, together with biological observations of UV erythema and inducible COX, informed distinct later programs. These are different kinds of inspiration; no common natural scaffold is asserted.

steps.description: Stone tasted willow bark, investigated it as a possible remedy and reported clinical observations in intermittent fever.
Chemists isolated salicin and studied salicylic acid, itself manufactured and used medicinally; acetylation produced acetylsalicylic acid, marketed as aspirin.

A separate ibuprofen program sought an improvement on aspirin's observed effects, using a UV-erythema model, testing new chemical series and selecting a propionic-acid candidate through activity and safety observations.
Recognition of distinct COX isoforms inspired selective inhibition; medicinal chemistry of established anti-inflammatory diarylheterocycles and subsequent tests of diarylpyrazoles led to celecoxib.

A different non-carboxylate discovery program investigated active indandione leads and their limitations, developed active longer-lived benzothiazine structures and produced an oxicam series; meloxicam is a later member of that branch.

design.description: Researchers isolated and chemically transformed salicylate-related substances and acetylated salicylic acid; synthesized and screened several distinct phenylalkanoic-acid series and selected ibuprofen on biological activity and tolerability observations; developed active, longer-lived non-carboxylate oxicam structures; and used selective COX-2 testing and diarylpyrazole structure–activity work to change target selectivity, architecture and pharmacokinetic properties in the celecoxib program. These were substantial chemical and pharmacological design contributions developed alongside or from observed effects and relationships.

circumstances.description: Stone reported accidentally tasting willow bark and then deliberately prepared and tested it. The ibuprofen, oxicam and celecoxib research programs deliberately screened or modified candidate compounds; these statements apply to those named events, not to every discovery in the family.

classes.name: Beta-adrenoceptor blockers

starting.description: Clinical and physiological observations suggested reducing adrenaline-driven cardiac demand. Known endogenous catecholamine effects and the selective agonist isoprenaline supplied the functional/structural clue, followed by informative DCI observations and deliberate antagonist development.

inspiration.description: Clinical angina/adrenaline relationships, cardiac-demand physiology, noradrenaline-related isoprenaline activity, receptor reasoning and DCI findings supplied complementary inspirations. Rational antagonist design is preserved as a contribution.

steps.description: Clinical/physiological problems and adrenergic responses motivated the beta-blockade goal.
The isoprenaline structure was the starting chemical clue for planned agonist-to-antagonist analogue exploration.
DCI findings and improved assays revealed useful antagonist/partial-agonist behavior and motivated pronethalol.
Further deliberate chemistry sought improved safety/activity and produced propranolol, helping establish the class.

design.description: Investigators deliberately sought a new pharmacological action, changing an agonist-related structure into an antagonist and improving the assay, potency and safety. These are substantial design/function changes, not merely delivery modifications, within an observation-inspired programme.

circumstances.description: The project and chemical changes were planned; DCI's tissue-dependent activity and its reassessment supplied a named unexpected contribution.

classes.name: Selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors
classes.scopeNote: Basis scope: diphenhydramine-to-nisoxetine; extension to atomoxetine inferred.

starting.description: In the documented Lilly founding branch, diphenhydramine's observed potentiation of noradrenaline and inhibition of monoamine uptake suggested antidepressant potential and led to analogue synthesis and testing that yielded selective nisoxetine. Earlier observed neuronal uptake and imipramine's inhibition provided wider context. Documented class support is bounded to this founding branch; its extension to atomoxetine is inferred and the initial analogue-selection chronology remains unknown.

inspiration.description: Neuronal noradrenaline uptake and its inhibition by the existing antidepressant imipramine and the antihistamine diphenhydramine.

steps.description: Researchers observed neuronal uptake of noradrenaline and its inhibition by an existing antidepressant.
A separate early selective-noradrenaline inhibitor effort produced maprotiline.

Diphenhydramine's observed monoamine-uptake inhibition informed Lilly analogue synthesis; screening and structure-activity analysis produced nisoxetine, which was tested for selective noradrenaline uptake inhibition.

A 1982 original study reported selective norepinephrine uptake inhibition by LY139603, the more potent negative isomer of a phenoxypropylamine racemate. A later paper identifies LY139603 as atomoxetine, and a review describes its structural relationship to nisoxetine; these sources do not establish the exact development sequence between the compounds.

design.description: Researchers synthesized and screened diphenhydramine analogues, used structure-activity analysis to identify selective nisoxetine, and later compared the uptake inhibition of the optical isomers of a related methylphenoxy analogue. The precise rationale and chronological synthesis steps for selecting atomoxetine are not established by the sources read.

circumstances.description: The Lilly analogue synthesis and mouse and uptake testing were planned; this does not establish whether the earlier pharmacological observations were anticipated.

classes.name: Statins (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors)

starting.description: Cholesterol/disease biology motivated a deliberate microbial-inhibitor search. Observed inhibition of cholesterol synthesis by fungal ML-236 metabolites supplied the working lead from which the statin class developed.

inspiration.description: Fungal metabolites with observed cholesterol-synthesis inhibition, within a pathway/disease-motivated investigation.

steps.description: The investigators sought microbial substances that specifically inhibited cholesterol synthesis.
The search yielded ML-236 metabolites from Penicillium citrinum, opening the fungal statin lineage.
The class later included semisynthetic and synthetic members, preserving its founding natural-product ancestry at class level.
Endo identifies lovastatin's 1987 approval as the first commercial statin, followed by the later members summarized in the conclusion.

design.description: Development established natural, semisynthetic and wholly synthetic later statins. Those chemical routes are later contributions within the observation-led class; this bounded record does not reconstruct each analogue's modifications.

circumstances.description: The documented microbial search deliberately sought inhibitors of cholesterol synthesis. The selected passages do not establish an accidental class-founding finding.

classes.name: H1 antihistamines

starting.description: Observed physiological activities of histamine, acetylcholine and adrenaline, together with known pharmacological antagonists of the latter two, motivated Bovet and Staub to test compounds for comparable antihistamine activity.

inspiration.description: The founding clue was the activity of histamine and the observed antagonism of other biologically active mediators, a functional biological analogy rather than a claim of histamine scaffold inheritance. Later, the phenothiazine branch also drew on observed antihistamine effects in screened synthetic compounds.

steps.description: Bovet and Staub deliberately sought a histamine antagonist on the basis of prior mediator and antagonist observations and tested candidate compounds.
The early antihistamine was not clinically usable because of toxicity; later phenylethylenediamine research and Antergan established a useful class, followed by a variety of structural types.

The pre-existing phenothiazine-amine chemical series entered antihistamine screens; observed activity and toxicity guided selection of promethazine, a distinct structural branch. Halpern and Hamburger separately report experiments on its pharmacological effects.

Second-generation work sought fewer adverse effects and produced more selective, less centrally penetrating drugs; metabolite and enantiomer relationships distinguish later branches without establishing each discovery decision.

design.description: Researchers synthesized and tested multiple structural families, selected active and less toxic phenothiazines, established clinically useful antihistamines and later made structural changes associated with greater selectivity, longer duration and reduced brain penetration.

circumstances.description: Bovet and Staub's search and testing for a histamine antagonist were planned; this does not classify every subsequent branch discovery as planned.

classes.name: Macrolide antibiotics
classes.scopeNote: Basis scope: erythromycin-derived lineage; first-screen chronology and macrolide priority unresolved.

starting.description: Within the erythromycin-derived lineage, active microbial erythromycin A supplied a working parent for deliberate derivative programs. inspiration.description: Antibacterial activity of the erythromycin-producing soil actinomycete and its natural product; later derivatives were made from the already active antibiotic.

steps.description: A soil isolate produced measurable antibacterial material, which the inventors cultured and isolated as erythromycin.

Erythromycin A was chemically modified into the cohort agents clarithromycin and azithromycin. Researchers sought changes in acid stability, pharmacokinetics and antibacterial spectrum; an erythromycin-derived aza-macrolide series added nitrogen to a 15-membered ring.

design.description: Researchers cultivated and purified the natural antibiotic, then chemically modified erythromycin A to obtain semisynthetic derivatives. In the aza-macrolide series, inserting nitrogen and expanding the ring generated new structures with altered antibacterial spectra as well as pharmacokinetic aims.

circumstances.description: The later search for chemically modified erythromycin derivatives with altered spectrum and improved properties was deliberate; the circumstances of first detection are not established by the patent sections read.

starting.description: Before the reported 1962 synthesis, GABA had been observed to depress spinal-neuron excitability. Retrospective accounts describe the synthesis of a GABA derivative intended for central inhibition and improved brain access, and explicitly link later antispastic introduction to expected mimicry of endogenous GABA; a contemporary clinical paper discusses GABA's spinal inhibitory effects when introducing baclofen. These observations support an inferred development from GABA's known inhibitory biology; they do not identify the particular experiment or conference content that triggered Keberle's synthesis.

inspiration.description: Endogenous GABA and its observed inhibitory physiological effects; the specific experiment and conference content that informed Keberle remain unestablished.

steps.description: Curtis recalls that experiments beginning in 1958 found that applied GABA depressed spinal-neuron excitability, although its role as a spinal inhibitory transmitter was then uncertain.
Retrospective accounts describe synthesis of a GABA analogue intended to access the brain and exert inhibitory action; the inventor's exact initiating observation is not identified.
The 1969 inventor patent describes the chlorophenyl-substituted amino acid family and centrally inhibitory and muscle-relaxant activity; the history also recounts development toward antispastic use.

Clinical investigators discussed GABA's inhibitory effects on spinal neurons and reflexes when introducing baclofen; a 1971 placebo-controlled crossover trial reported greater improvement with the derivative.
Subsequent physiological testing associated baclofen with a bicuculline-insensitive GABA response, and the group named the receptor GABA-B in 1981.

design.description: Chemists synthesized a beta-para-chlorophenyl derivative of GABA with the aim of enabling central activity; the realized extent of brain penetration is separate from that aim.

circumstances.description: The described deliberate stage is the synthesis of GABA derivatives intended for central inhibitory activity, not a claim that all subsequent findings were planned.

classes.name: Glucocorticoids

starting.description: Adrenal-insufficiency physiology and the effects of adrenal extracts initiated cortical-hormone investigation. Separately, remission of rheumatoid arthritis during jaundice, pregnancy and some vaccine reactions led Hench to seek a protective substance. A reported protective effect of adrenal compound E against animal vaccine reactions helped motivate a planned arthritis test. This hypothesis did not prove that compound E caused the naturally observed remissions, and arthritis benefit of crude adrenal extract had not been established.

inspiration.description: Adrenal insufficiency and extract effects, clinical remission during jaundice, pregnancy or vaccine reactions, and a hormone isolated from adrenal cortex supplied related biological and clinical leads.

steps.description: Adrenal-cortex extracts produced beneficial effects in adrenal insufficiency; researchers isolated and studied individual adrenal steroids, including compound E.

Hench's observed remissions and hypothesis of substance X, together with Kendall's animal observation on compound E and vaccine reactions, prompted a planned trial of compound E after synthesis made it available.

Researchers modified the working adrenal hormones to alter steroid activity, producing prednisolone and prednisone and, with further substitutions, triamcinolone; hydrocortisone also became available for topical use.

Researchers extended established topical steroid effects to inhaled treatment of inflamed airways, reported clinical use of beclomethasone aerosol, and subsequently selected other steroid structures for altered local and systemic activity.

design.description: Researchers prepared and clinically tested compound E, then modified active steroid structures, including ring-A unsaturation and substitutions at carbons 9 and 16, to change pharmacological effects. They formulated steroids for systemic, skin and inhaled administration and later selected structures with different local versus systemic activity. These are substantial chemical, pharmacological and formulation contributions built on working hormone effects, not evidence that the founding class was designed from scratch.

circumstances.description: Hench and Kendall planned the compound E rheumatoid-arthritis test; the breadth of subsequent therapeutic applications surprised many researchers.

Cope and Jack directly support selected structural and topical-to-inhaled developments, not a separate origin or detailed synthesis for every later cohort member.
The inhaled-drug evidence describes selected later examples and recollections, not an exhaustive priority history or a guarantee of absence of systemic adverse effects.

Detailed development histories of individual later analogues and priority for every inhaled corticosteroid are outside this class-level collection.

classes.name: Beta2-adrenoceptor agonists

starting.description: The salbutamol programme started from the observed bronchodilator action and short duration of isoprenaline, pursuing a longer-lasting analogue; unexpected tissue-selective activity in AH3021 helped establish the selective series. A separate formoterol-related chemistry programme likewise built on isoproterenol's known effects and established selective analogues.

inspiration.description: In the broader history, observed bronchodilator effects of endogenous adrenaline preceded synthetic agonists; the Jack programme specifically worked from isoprenaline's known bronchodilator action and short duration and observed selective effects of AH3021 on bronchial versus cardiac preparations. The formoterol-related programme cited the effects and limitations of isoproterenol and established selective analogues.

steps.description: The team aimed to improve the duration of an existing effective inhaled bronchodilator, isoprenaline, by making non-catechol analogues.
Testing AH3021 revealed unexpected tissue selectivity; the subsequent analogue AH3365 was salbutamol.
The contemporary salbutamol report compared bronchial and cardiac responses and duration against earlier agonists in animal and tissue tests; selectivity was assay- and route-dependent.

In a separate reported chemistry programme, researchers built on existing bronchodilators and tested modified catecholamine and terbutaline analogues, selecting BD-40-A, later identified as formoterol. A review reports that its prolonged action became apparent after inhalation in patients; a 1989 clinical paper summarizes prior studies of that effect.

A later programme sought longer action by optimizing salbutamol analogues with extended non-polar substituents, producing salmeterol. A subsequent salmeterol-derived series used its observed metabolism as a design clue and yielded vilanterol, according to an abstract-only discoverer account.

design.description: Medicinal chemists altered the catechol functionality and developed analogue series around known working agonists, including a formylamino-substituted formoterol-related series; another programme extended non-polar substituents on salbutamol analogues to seek a longer-acting selective agonist. Vilanterol work additionally altered a salmeterol side chain in pursuit of metabolic and duration properties.

circumstances.description: A longer-acting isoprenaline analogue was sought deliberately; the marked bronchial-versus-heart selectivity of AH3021 was unexpectedly observed during testing, according to Jack. The separate formoterol-related chemistry paper explicitly describes a planned search for selective, potent bronchodilators.

classes.name: Muscarinic receptor antagonists

starting.description: Historical practitioners reported relief of asthma with Datura preparations before atropine isolation. Later work developed antimuscarinics from the known plant alkaloid atropine in response to useful effects and limiting toxicity; the evidence does not show that this particular 1811 report directly caused ipratropium design. Separately, bladder-selectivity programs developed compounds from known synthetic muscarinic leads and tested receptor binding and selectivity.

inspiration.description: Atropine and scopolamine were plant alkaloids with historical therapeutic use. Later respiratory design responded to benefits and toxicity of atropine; bladder-selectivity work used existing synthetic antagonist-related leads and tested receptor binding.

steps.description: Traditional preparations containing belladonna-type alkaloids were used medicinally; atropine was isolated and used in medicine in the 19th century.
Christie reported clinical relief from Datura smoke in asthma cases, an early account of the plant-use tradition, while also noting adverse effects and recurrence.
Dale's 1914 experiments distinguished atropine-sensitive muscarine-like physiological actions from nicotine-like actions, supplying a later pharmacological distinction.
Limited by systemic effects of atropine, later workers pursued less-absorbed anticholinergics; ipratropium is a quaternary N-isopropyl atropine derivative for inhalation.

A bladder-selectivity program pursued new benzhydrylcarbamates related to an existing 4-DAMP-derived antagonist. The investigators tested a quinuclidin-3-yl benzhydrylcarbamate with strong muscarinic binding but little M3-versus-M2 selectivity.
A discoverer retrospective identifies solifenacin as a conformationally restricted analogue of a known quinuclidinyl benzhydrylcarbamate antagonist, pursued for bladder selectivity.

design.description: Atropine was modified at its nitrogen to produce a quaternary analogue with low absorption for respiratory use. Bladder-selectivity research used carbamate substitutions in known antagonist-related structures; solifenacin was designed by conformational restriction of a named quinuclidinyl benzhydrylcarbamate lead, whose exact identity with 1998 compound 7l is not confirmed.

circumstances.description: The later efforts to find a less systemically absorbed anticholinergic and to improve bladder selectivity were purposeful; whether the initial traditional discovery was planned or unexpected is not established.

classes.name: Thiazide and thiazide-like diuretics

starting.description: An earlier report of sulfanilamide-associated diuresis and acidemia supplied background for carbonic-anhydrase-inhibitor research, according to a later review. In Beyer's directed salt-excreting programme, a carboxyl-substituted synthetic sulfanilamide analogue yielded chloride excretion; Beyer identifies this observed lead as the reason for more work on saluretic sulfonamides, culminating in chlorothiazide.

inspiration.description: Renal salt and water physiology informed the therapeutic objective; observations of sulfanilamide-associated diuresis and of a synthetic analogue's chloride-excreting effect supplied background and a specific working lead, respectively.

steps.description: A later review traces the research background to an observed diuretic effect and acidemia with sulfanilamide and subsequent carbonic anhydrase work. Beyer's team sought a practical oral agent to promote salt and water excretion, guided by physiological reasoning and comparative renal testing.
A carboxyl-substituted sulfanilamide analogue caused chloride excretion, strengthening the work on saluretic sulfonamides.

Structure–activity research in that line culminated in chlorothiazide; the original chemistry report describes synthesizing the benzothiadiazine series and their saluretic effects, and subsequent work included hydrochlorothiazide.

The family came to include thiazides such as bendroflumethiazide and hydrochlorothiazide and structurally diverse thiazide-like sulfonamides such as chlorthalidone and indapamide, which lack the benzothiadiazine ring; a review summarizes their development together without supplying each programme's founding steps.

In a distinct thiazide-like example, a 1961 clinical study identified chlorthalidone as a Geigy sulphonyl benzophenone derivative and described a longer-acting sodium- and chloride-excreting response similar to chlorothiazide; this is evidence of the established branch, not its founding rationale.

design.description: Researchers set a salt-excretion objective, made and compared sulfanilamide analogues, measured renal responses, and developed the saluretic lead into sulfamylbenzothiadiazine structures including chlorothiazide and related thiazides.

circumstances.description: Beyer describes a deliberate programme seeking salt excretion. A later review calls the earlier sulfanilamide observation accidental and the chloride-versus-bicarbonate effect of chlorothiazide unexpected. The exact expectations at each experimental stage are not resolved by these differing accounts.

classes.name: Peripheral local-anesthetic antitussives

starting.description: Airway local anesthetics' cough-suppressing effects and experimental links between lung inflation and cough directed research toward an agent that would anesthetize pulmonary-distention-sensitive vagal fibers, according to contemporary clinical authors and a later review.

inspiration.description: Observed suppression of cough during local anesthesia and experimental relationships between inspiratory lung distention and cough intensity.

steps.description: Prior clinical effects of local anesthetics and experimental respiratory physiology directed research toward a peripheral antitussive, according to contemporary clinical authors and a later review.

Separately, a 1955 Matter patent described preparation of a p-butylaminobenzoate polyethoxy ester and pharmacological properties of the broader ester group. The patent does not document a cough rationale or establish whether this particular preparation followed the physiological observations.
Bucher investigated benzonatate's effects on lung stretch receptors, according to the review; 1958 clinical investigators tested Tessalon against induced cough and in patients.

design.description: Matter described preparing polyethoxy esters including the p-butylaminobenzoate member; the 1958 clinicians described polyethylene glycol replacing a diethylaminoethanol residue. Neither source establishes why the chemist first selected this exact structure for cough.

circumstances.description: The contemporary clinical report describes research directed toward selective anesthesia of pulmonary-distention-sensitive vagal fibers. It does not specify whether the first observation of the compound's antitussive effect was unexpected.

The peripheral target was a stated development rationale, not definitive proof of a unique clinical mechanism; the 1969 review recounts a competing central interpretation (E8).
conflicts: The 1969 review reports peripheral effects but notes that Sell, Lindner, and Jahn 1958 interpreted benzonatate's antitussive action as mainly central; the doses needed for consistent effects in those experiments were toxic, according to the review (E8). This mechanism dispute does not contradict the documented historical starting rationale.

In the 1958 induced-cough report, the authors describe subject 4 as unaltered, whereas their Table I lists 18 efforts before and 16 after; their wording and displayed counts should not be conflated (E7).
gaps: Bucher and Jacot 1951 and Bucher 1956 were located by metadata but their original texts were not read; their findings are attributed to the reviews (S1, S4).
The Sell, Lindner, and Jahn 1958 mechanistic study (S7) was not read directly; its characterization is attributed to S4.
The chemist's motive for selecting the particular structure and the exact transition from ester chemistry to cough testing are not established by the patent or clinical report.

classes.name: Histamine analogues for vertigo

starting.description: Histamine's vasodilating properties motivated its clinical use for episodic vertigo and Ménière's disease; clinicians reported apparent benefits. According to retrospective accounts, these experiences and the difficulty of repeated injections supplied the setting for a search for an oral alternative in which betahistine was found. Campbell's particular cases are examples of the historical observations, not proven triggers of that search.

inspiration.description: The working clue was the vasoactive and reported therapeutic effects of histamine, an endogenous molecule, in vertigo/Ménière's disease. Betahistine is a histamine analogue; its later receptor characterization should not be projected backward as the original rationale.

steps.description: The reported vasodilating effect of histamine provided a rationale for its use in episodic vertigo and inner-ear disease. Campbell later recorded perceived responses to injected histamine in eleven Ménière's patients, while warning about the small series and natural fluctuations.

According to retrospective reports, prior histamine treatment and difficulty with oral use and repeated injections led to a search for an oral alternative; betahistine, an orally active histamine analogue, was found. The original developers and chemical-development sequence are not established by these accounts.

Frew and Menon subsequently investigated betahistine in a placebo-controlled crossover study for Ménière's symptoms and reported improvement; later systematic review found the included betahistine efficacy evidence uncertain. Historical use and current effectiveness are distinct questions.

design.description: Researchers found and developed an orally active, histamine-like alternative for a treatment previously given by injection. The record does not establish whether betahistine was newly synthesized for this program or repurposed, the specific structural-design choices, or what the original team knew about later H1/H3 receptor actions.

circumstances.description: Frew and Menon's account describes a search for an orally administered alternative to histamine. This identifies the search as intentional; it does not establish whether the initial chemical discovery or therapeutic effect was expected or accidental.

classes.name: Loop diuretics

starting.description: In the sulfamoyl line, sulfanilamide treatment was observed to produce metabolic acidosis and alkaline urine, followed by recognition of mild diuresis and development of related active sulfonamide diuretics; a retrospective history links modification of that active series to furosemide. In the distinct ethacrynic-acid line, already active mercurial diuretics, including merbaphen and mersalyl, supplied functional and structural models for nonmercurial compounds. Wilson recounts a clinical rise in urine output with merbaphen. These are distinct observed drug-effect starting points, not one shared chemical scaffold.

inspiration.description: Clinical effects of synthetic sulfanilamide and mercurial diuretics initiated or informed distinct precursor lines; subsequently active sulfonamide compounds and furosemide were working drug leads. This counts as biological inspiration under the approved broad observation-led definition, not as a claim that the final drugs were isolated from nature.

steps.description: A clinical sulfanilamide side effect and subsequent recognition of mild diuresis preceded development of related sulfamoyl diuretics, including later high-ceiling agents in Feit's retrospective.

After sulfonamide-related compounds were studied for chloride excretion, Sneader links an acidic-group substitution in the dichlorphenamide-related series to furosemide. The Hoechst patent describes synthesis of the furfurylamino compound associated with furosemide and compares diuretic effects in rats with a benzothiadiazine.

Using established furosemide and related active compounds as reference points, Feit and colleagues moved an amino substituent and screened variants in dogs; Feit then altered the 4-position and selected compound 111, bumetanide, for further study.

In a separate branch, observed diuresis with the mercurial merbaphen preceded established mercury diuretics; a later account coauthored by a discoverer identifies mercurial phenoxyacetic-acid diuretics as models leading to the nonmercurial ethacrynic-acid series.

After ethacrynic acid existed, human physiological experiments suggested an important action in the ascending loop of Henle; this localization supports its class connection and must not be projected back as the initial design inspiration.

design.description: Researchers synthesized and tested new sulfamoyl structures, with a carboxyl substitution described in the furosemide history; Feit and colleagues moved an amino group, modified the 4-position and selected bumetanide from active variants. A different program used mercurial drug models to develop nonmercurial phenoxyacetic-acid structures including ethacrynic acid. These changed chemistry and pharmacologic activity, not only delivery; the read sources do not establish an initial loop-target design.

circumstances.description: Feit's retrospective describes the antecedent sulfanilamide clinical side effect as chance; Wilson identifies metabolic acidosis and alkaline urine among the initial observations. The later Hoechst comparative testing and Feit team's structure–activity synthesis and dog screening were planned investigations. This does not assert that the individual syntheses or every observed result were accidental.

classes.name: Opioid receptor agonists and partial agonists

starting.description: The natural-opiate branch began with the recognized therapeutic effects of opium, followed by isolation and testing of morphine; the first observer is not established. In a distinct synthetic antispasmodic program, pethidine's morphine-like analgesia was unexpectedly observed, then developed. Methadone's series was pursued against the background of known morphine and pethidine effects and structural ideas; the peripheral branch drew on opioids' observed bowel effects.

inspiration.description: Opium and its observed effects preceded morphine isolation. A thebaine-derived program sought to improve on known codeine activity and selected candidates through biological tests. For peripheral action, the useful bowel effects of opium and morphine, and later observations with synthetic diphenoxylate, informed the search for a better-separated antidiarrheal. Pethidine's unexpected morphine-like analgesic effect was discovered in an antispasmodic program; the methadone series was connected with comparative morphine and pethidine activity and a structural hypothesis. Theoretical chemistry here builds on known active substances rather than establishing activity from scratch.

steps.description: Opium preparations were used for analgesia before modern receptor concepts; the first observation and the identity of the original observer are not established by this retrospective.
Sertürner isolated morphine from opium and tested its opium-like effects; later opioid work included morphine analogues such as hydrocodone.

Seeking an improvement on the known analgesic codeine, Bentley and colleagues modified thebaine-derived chemistry; Lewis and colleagues used pharmacological observations and dependence testing to select buprenorphine, later characterized as a mu partial agonist.

In a separate synthetic branch, pethidine's morphine-like analgesic effect was unexpectedly observed during an antispasmodic search and developed as an analgesic; diphenoxylate, chemically related to pethidine, later provided an antidiarrheal lead.

Bockmühl and Ehrhart described a separate synthetic-compound program in relation to the established morphine model and morphine-like pethidine, noting a shared carbon feature while emphasizing that their series did not simply copy a fragment of morphine. A later historical reconstruction connects that program and animal testing to Va 10820, later methadone.

Building on known bowel effects of opioids and subsequent tests of the synthetic antidiarrheal diphenoxylate, researchers screened for greater separation of antidiarrheal and central effects and identified loperamide in a new series.

design.description: Extraction and testing isolated an active principle. Medicinal chemists then made morphine analogues and thebaine-derived compounds with substantial structural changes; biological testing selected buprenorphine, subsequently characterized as a partial agonist. In the methadone series chemists devised new synthetic structures informed by comparisons with morphine and pethidine and tested their biological activity. A later antidiarrheal program sought a different distribution of activity, emphasizing intestinal effects over measured central effects. These were substantial changes in structure or pharmacology, not merely delivery changes.

circumstances.description: The buprenorphine precursor program deliberately sought an improvement on codeine, and the peripheral program deliberately screened for more selective antidiarrheals. By contrast, pethidine's analgesic effect was reported as unexpected during a planned antispasmodic search. These descriptions refer to those specific stages, not every member of the class.

classes.name: Norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitors

starting.description: A retrospective describes the program's goal of an antidepressant with a distinct pharmacologic profile and improved safety and tolerability; it does not establish the particular biological observation or design idea that prompted the program.

inspiration.description: not_reported

steps.description: A retrospective describes a targeted program seeking an antidepressant with a different pharmacological profile and improved tolerability; its initiating inspiration is unspecified.
The inventor's patent describes synthesis of the chlorine-substituted aminopropiophenone and reports antidepressant-screen activity relative to stimulation.
The compound was investigated in a controlled healthy-volunteer comparison, and further clinical work was reported underway; the paper recounts earlier animal screening.
Subsequent laboratory experiments reported weak inhibition of dopamine and norepinephrine uptake in rat synaptosomes; the full study was not accessed.
A 2005 review described the later dual norepinephrine/dopamine reuptake inhibitor classification; earlier authors had been cautious about dopamine uptake alone explaining antidepressant activity.

design.description: The inventor synthesized a meta-chloro aminopropiophenone and described its fluoro analogue, in a development program retrospectively described as seeking a distinct antidepressant profile. The source passages do not establish the original target-based design rationale or a causal lead.

circumstances.description: The retrospective characterizes the program's goal of developing an antidepressant as targeted; it does not say whether the specific active compound was anticipated or unexpectedly found.

classes.name: 5-HT1A partial-agonist anxiolytics

starting.description: The original psychotropic series was developed from the observed tranquilizer-like activity of an earlier synthetic compound. Subsequently, behavioral calming by the existing synthetic psychotropic buspirone supplied an anxiolytic clue: a researcher on the cited monkey study states that anxiety trials followed its activity in a predictive aggressive-monkey model. A later retrospective separately describes reduced agitation during feeding; its relationship to the formal test and its exact chronology are not established.

inspiration.description: Observed psychotropic effects in an earlier synthetic cyclic-imide series guided the original chemical work; buspirone's behavioral effects in monkeys subsequently guided anxiety testing. This does not claim isolation of the compound from a natural source.

steps.description: In psychotropic research preceding the anxiolytic indication, an active earlier phenylpiperazine cyclic imide was used as a starting point for a modified heteroaryl series; the researchers sought stronger and more selective activity and screened the products.
The already-synthesized psychotropic buspirone was observed to calm aggressive rhesus monkeys; Taylor says performance in a predictive behavioral model prompted testing for anxiety.
The inventors reported earlier major-tranquilizer-like work and presented a distinct anxiolytic use, with an open human anxiety evaluation.
After buspirone's behavioral and clinical testing, a company team varied the aromatic group, connecting chain and cyclic imide to study the structure-activity relationships of its analogues.

In 1985, after anxiolytic development was underway, binding studies linked buspirone and a related anxiolytic to 5-HT1A receptors; by 1988 Taylor reviewed functional evidence for partial agonism. This later mechanism is not the documented initial drug-design rationale.

design.description: Investigators altered an active phenylpiperazine cyclic-imide series to seek improved psychotropic potency and selectivity, used a predictive behavioral model to select buspirone for anxiety trials, and later varied aromatic, linker and imide regions to study analogues.

circumstances.description: Gribkoff and Kaczmarek characterize the feeding observation during antipsychotic development and anxiolytic discovery as serendipitous. Taylor states that the later decision to begin anxiety trials followed a predictive monkey test and was not serendipitous. The different events and their relationship cannot be fully reconciled from these sources.

classes.name: Angiotensin II receptor blockers

starting.description: Takeda researchers observed diuresis from synthetic CV-2198, then blood-pressure lowering at doses without diuresis. On investigating this effect they found angiotensin II antagonism in rabbit vessels and developed related antagonists including CV-2961. DuPont built on weak, selective antagonism of related Takeda benzylimidazoles. Angiotensin II physiology and prior peptide antagonists supplied the biological context.

inspiration.description: CV-2198's diuretic and non-diuretic blood-pressure effects led to a demonstrated synthetic angiotensin antagonist series. The renin–angiotensin system and endogenous angiotensin II supplied biological context and a later molecular-modeling reference.

steps.description: Angiotensin II physiology and peptide antagonists provided biological context and exposed limitations for chronic therapy.

Takeda observed diuretic and independent blood-pressure effects of CV-2198, investigated the mechanism and found angiotensin II antagonism; related structure–activity work produced CV-2961. A 1982 patent reports angiotensin II antagonism by imidazole-acetic acid derivatives in rabbit vessels and rats.
DuPont evaluated two patented Takeda benzylimidazoles and observed weak selective competitive receptor antagonism, despite not confirming the reported potency.
Peptide-guided lead enlargement and structure–activity work generated more potent but orally inactive phthalamic acids, orally active biphenyls and the tetrazole-containing losartan.
Further Takeda work on benzimidazole acids and ester prodrugs led to candesartan and candesartan cilexetil, with a changed ring system and improved oral delivery.

Later class designs retained a relation to the losartan prototype while changing the active architecture, including an amino-acid-derived replacement of the imidazole in valsartan and an imidazolinone in irbesartan.

After oral losartan was reported, Sankyo screened synthesized imidazoles and optimized a potent, long-acting lead into olmesartan; its medoxomil ester was selected to improve oral availability. An earlier paper's abstract reports testing of related acids and oral esters.

design.description: Researchers separated diuresis from antagonist effects, modeled synthetic antagonists against endogenous angiotensin II, and changed structures to improve affinity, selectivity, oral activity and duration. Later benzimidazole, imidazolinone and amino-acid-derived active structures represent architecture changes, while esterification of candesartan and olmesartan was a prodrug delivery change.

circumstances.description: The investigation of CV-2198's blood-pressure effect, subsequent antagonist structure–activity studies, and DuPont lead optimization were deliberate. Whether the initial diuretic or blood-pressure finding was unexpected is not established by the retrospective.

classes.name: Dibenzazepine anticonvulsants

starting.description: According to Sato and colleagues' historical account, anticonvulsant activity was observed in the synthetic compound N-carbamyl-iminodibenzyl (G26301); Geigy then continued research on related derivatives, leading to Tegretol (G32883, carbamazepine). Morel and Häfliger's 1956 patent independently reports anticonvulsant activity for the precursor, without describing its assay. The laboratory decision process is not directly documented here.

inspiration.description: The inferred functional starting clue is the reported anticonvulsant effect of synthetic G26301, not isolation of a natural scaffold. The histories link the active precursor and subsequent derivatives in the same line of work, but do not directly record the researchers' motivation for choosing carbamazepine.

steps.description: Sato and colleagues report the discovery of anticonvulsant activity in Morel's G26301, and the 1956 precursor patent reports that activity without providing the seizure-testing method.

Sato and colleagues say Geigy continued derivative research that led to the iminostilbene derivative Tegretol; Meijer and colleagues also describe the compounds as part of one line of enquiry. Sato's stated synthesis year is contradicted by the 1960 patent.
Schindler's 1960 patent describes preparation of 5-carbamyl iminostilbene and asserts anticonvulsant activity for the azepines, without reporting a biological test.

The historical chapter describes animal results for G32883 as more promising than for G26301; Sato and colleagues' public 1965 abstract reports clinical administration in 20 cases, including difficult-to-control epilepsy. Neither the original animal methods nor complete clinical paper were read.

design.description: Researchers investigated iminodibenzyl-related derivatives; the carbamazepine compound has an unsaturated iminostilbene ring rather than G26301's saturated iminodibenzyl bridge. Schindler's patent describes preparation from iminostilbene, not direct conversion of G26301. The sources do not establish a particular claimed improvement as the reason for this structural change.

circumstances.description: The documented event is the deliberate derivative research and chemical preparation, not the circumstances of the first G26301 anticonvulsant observation. S2 calls carbamazepine's later anticonvulsant finding chance, but its chronology conflicts with S3; the original discovery circumstances are not established.
